title: Public Operating Sovereignty Covenant
question: What conditions make public-platform exit a durable redistribution of operating power rather than a contract change, partial migration, or new dependency?

systems.title: Homes for Ukraine: Palantir-hosted service to public Share service
observed_chain: migration of three years of operational data
user research, quality assurance, training, and phased transition
continuing Share operation across local-authority workflow
supports: bounded observed substitution rather than a paper exit clause
public multidisciplinary build and operating capacity
migration of a live workflow and historical operational data
continued public service after supplier exit
reported public ownership of replacement code and data
does_not_support: complete deletion of every supplier-held copy or derivative
independent verification of all savings, performance, and usability claims
guest or sponsor co-governance over purpose, categories, or thresholds
universal substitutability of Palantir across enterprise deployments
R7 value recovery from the prior public contribution

systems.title: NHS bounded product transition and continuing enterprise platform
observed_chain: formal transition and exit instruments for bounded Foundry-supported products
separate larger Federated Data Platform procurement and award
formal public data and governance safeguards
practical enterprise substitution and completed exit remain unproved
supports: exit and transition can be contractually specified at a bounded product level
formal transition rights do not by themselves establish completed migration
product-level movement can coexist with a larger continuing enterprise dependency
scope must be frozen before assigning R5
does_not_support: independent public operation of the entire platform layer
complete data, schema, interface, model, and accreditation portability
absence of public safeguards or competition

systems.title: NGC2 alternate implementations and common-baseline concentration
observed_chain: multiple prototype awards and divisional implementations
Anduril lead responsibility for a common data baseline
Palantir and Raft differentiated integration roles
supports: program-level plurality and an operated alternative implementation
public customer authority over mission and integration
the need to test substitutability at each component and interface
a common layer can remain concentrated inside a plural program
does_not_support: substitutability of the common data baseline
completed exit from Anduril, Palantir, or Raft components
durable public operation without the named vendors

public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.requirement: Freeze the exact functions, users, consequences, service levels, and deployment boundaries before and after exit.
public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.failure_state: A product, contract, or brand changes while the consequential function remains in the same practical custody.

public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.requirement: The public institution can export, validate, understand, and reuse complete data, schemas, lineage, logs, identifiers, relationships, and correction history.
public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.failure_state: Formal data title exists without a usable, complete, independently intelligible export.

public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.requirement: Workflows, rules, interfaces, models, thresholds, configuration, and action rights are documented and reproducible outside the incumbent platform.
public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.failure_state: The replacement preserves hidden dependence on proprietary workflow, model, ontology, API, or support knowledge.

public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.requirement: Security, accreditation, authorization, audit, incident response, and legal responsibility survive migration without an accountability gap.
public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.failure_state: A nominal replacement cannot lawfully or safely operate the consequential service.

public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.requirement: Public staff possess durable skills, documentation, budget, source or escrow rights, support capacity, and succession plans.
public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.failure_state: The service is formally public but depends on a small temporary team, outgoing contractor, or inaccessible tacit knowledge.

public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.requirement: Observed service continuity, errors, latency, outcomes, user burden, and total cost are compared before, during, and after exit.
public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.failure_state: Formal ownership improves while capability, continuity, rights, or outcomes materially deteriorate.

public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.requirement: Residual vendor access, copies, derivatives, credentials, support channels, licenses, and downstream processors are inventoried, terminated, deleted, or independently governed.
public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.failure_state: The old provider retains consequential custody or the ability to reconstruct, operate, or monetize the prior system.

public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.requirement: Fallback operations, failed migrations, rejected alternatives, successor vendors, and the no-platform path remain in the denominator.
public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.failure_state: One successful cutover is narrated without the costs, failures, alternatives, or emergency reversion path.

public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.requirement: Operational users and represented people can inspect, contest, pause, govern, and remedy the consequential replacement workflow.
public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.failure_state: Operating sovereignty returns to the public institution while affected people remain outside the objective function.

public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.requirement: Post-exit purpose, category, threshold, exception, termination, cost savings, learning, and residual value are governed and distributed through explicit public and affected-party rights.
public_operating_sovereignty_dimensions.failure_state: R5 public capacity is mistaken for R6 co-governance or R7 just value recovery.

adapter.name: Public Operating Sovereignty Covenant
minimum_rules: No R5 finding without an observed live cutover or independent parallel operation.
The incumbent and replacement must be compared at the same functional scope.
Data title must be separated from practical custody, intelligibility, and portability.
Source, schema, interface, model, workflow, security, and accreditation dependencies must be named.
A public institution must retain enough staff, budget, documentation, and authority to operate after turnover and administration change.
Residual vendor access, derivative data, support dependence, and deletion must be independently auditable.
Service continuity, performance, error, cost, and person-level outcomes must be measured before and after transition.
Failed migrations, fallbacks, and successor dependencies remain in the denominator.
R5 cannot generate R6 or R7 without separate governance and value-rights instruments.
pilot_packet: contract, deployment, transition, cutover, and termination dates
data, schema, lineage, model, interface, workflow, and log inventory
source-code, escrow, documentation, license, and IP rights
security, accreditation, incident, and continuity records
staffing, skills, budget, support, and succession plan
migration rehearsal, fallback, failure, and rollback records
pre/post performance, cost, error, and user-outcome measures
residual access, deletion, derivative, and processor audit
R6 governance and R7 value-distribution terms

propositions.claim: Homes for Ukraine Share supplies a bounded observed R5 public-platform substitution.
propositions.support: The official record describes an in-house build, historical-data migration, user transition, supplier exit, and continuing public operation.
counterevidence: the principal performance and savings account is official
complete residual-custody and deletion evidence is absent
long-run resilience after staff and administration change is not yet observed
propositions.falsifier: Independent records show the service could not operate without the prior supplier, the migration materially failed, or the public account omitted a controlling private dependency.
propositions.stopping_rule: Keep the result bounded to the exact Homes for Ukraine Share functions and dates.

propositions.claim: The current record closes independent long-run performance, full cost, resilience, and affected-person outcome claims for Share.
propositions.support: Continuing operation, user feedback, and reduced running cost are officially reported.
counterevidence: no independent matched performance audit is in the frozen record
guest and sponsor outcome evidence is incomplete
future staffing and maintenance durability remain open
propositions.falsifier: Independent audits and affected-person records confirm the reported continuity, cost, quality, and resilience over a durable interval.
propositions.stopping_rule: Do not convert an official delivery account into a complete outcome audit.

propositions.claim: Public ownership of replacement code and data by itself proves practical operating sovereignty.
propositions.support: Ownership is an important input to public capacity.
counterevidence: operation also depends on staff, knowledge, interfaces, security, support, accreditation, budget, and continuity
formal rights may be unusable without complete exports and documentation
propositions.falsifier: A bounded deployment shows that ownership alone, without the other operating capabilities, reliably produces independent continuity.
propositions.stopping_rule: Keep title, custody, capability, and governance as separate dimensions.

propositions.claim: The Share transition proves complete deletion of supplier-held data, derivatives, credentials, and residual access.
propositions.support: The public institution reports supplier-contract exit and migration.
counterevidence: no complete deletion certificate or derivative-data audit is in the frozen source set
processor, backup, support, and credential termination are not fully reconstructed
propositions.falsifier: Independent exit records establish complete inventory, revocation, deletion, derivative treatment, and audit closure.
propositions.stopping_rule: Do not infer deletion from contract exit or service cutover.

propositions.claim: Bounded NHS product transitions and exit contracts prove completed enterprise exit from the Federated Data Platform.
propositions.support: Formal transition and exit instruments exist for bounded services and products.
counterevidence: a separate larger FDP award and continuing enterprise platform exist
completed migration, enterprise data portability, and independent operation are not established
propositions.falsifier: A complete enterprise record shows the FDP functions, data, users, interfaces, models, accreditation, and responsibility migrated to an independently operated replacement.
propositions.stopping_rule: Do not move an exit claim across product and enterprise scopes.

propositions.claim: NGC2 alternate divisional implementations prove the common data baseline and every named component are substitutable.
propositions.support: Multiple teams and implementations remain in the public denominator.
counterevidence: the Army selected an Anduril-led common data baseline
Palantir and Raft hold differentiated integration roles
no completed component exit is observed
propositions.falsifier: Observed replacement records show the common baseline and each critical component can be swapped while preserving mission, data, accreditation, performance, and responsibility.
propositions.stopping_rule: Measure exit and substitution at the exact component and interface.

propositions.claim: One bounded Share exit proves universal Palantir substitutability.
propositions.support: The case demonstrates that at least one consequential public workflow can be rebuilt and operated publicly.
counterevidence: deployments differ in scope, data, ontology, integrations, accreditation, time pressure, and mission risk
other public systems show continuing enterprise dependence or only partial transition
propositions.falsifier: Matched completed exits across materially different Palantir deployments show comparable continuity, cost, rights, and public capacity.
propositions.stopping_rule: Treat every deployment as a separate exit proposition.

propositions.claim: R5 public operating capacity supplies R6 affected-party co-governance and R7 proportionate value recovery.
propositions.support: Public operation can create a better foundation for governance and public value retention.
counterevidence: no guest or sponsor authority over purpose, threshold, exception, or termination is established
cost savings and public ownership are not an affected-party residual-rights ledger
propositions.falsifier: Binding governance and value-distribution instruments connect represented people to post-exit decision rights and realized value.
propositions.stopping_rule: Do not import R6 or R7 from R5.

propositions.claim: APC-EXIT-01 is a complete observed answer in the public-platform domain.
propositions.support: The positive and control systems identify concrete capability, rights, continuity, residual-custody, and scope tests.
counterevidence: no one observed deployment closes every operating-sovereignty dimension
independent outcome, deletion, co-governance, and value evidence remain incomplete
propositions.falsifier: A pilot applying the adapter fails to preserve continuity, practical independence, evidence, affected-party rights, or public value.
propositions.stopping_rule: Keep the adapter at candidate design until one prospectively governed exit satisfies the complete packet.

current_result.strongest_positive_control: Homes for Ukraine Share supplies a bounded observed public build, migration, supplier exit, and continuing public operation.
current_result.strongest_fault_line: Product-level transition and program-level plurality do not prove enterprise or common-component substitutability.
current_result.largest_open_join: Independent long-run outcome audit, full residual-custody and deletion closure, durability after turnover, affected-party co-governance, and value recovery.
